curriculum.title: DepEd-authored MATATAG Araling Panlipunan, Grade 5
curriculum.officialAccess: 403 during this review; inspected the DepEd-authored PDF copy
curriculum.referenceLabels: Quarter and row locators, not official competency codes

limits: A mapped topic does not establish teaching adequacy or DepEd certification.
Existing 13 partial-depth findings remain open; new application activities do not automatically close them.
The 66 new activities are authored optional practice, not a replacement for all existing official quiz banks.
All story wording is retained by the shared short-reading renderer; shorter parts do not prove a Grade 5 reading level.
All four Chapter 3 missions now have prepared 30-question bank revisions; other official banks are preserved.

missions.title: Changes in Settlements and Housing
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we compare settlement and housing changes using evidence?
missions.why: Buildings can offer clues about materials and organisation. They do not automatically reveal every resident's experiences.
missions.application: Two dated housing examples use different materials. What can a comparison explain?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Education, Language, and Religious Life
missions.guidingQuestion: What is the difference between providing a learning material and showing who learned?
missions.why: Education, language and religious life involve access and responses. A book's existence does not establish that everyone could use it.
missions.application: A school record lists a teaching material. What needs further evidence?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Social Hierarchies and Everyday Experiences
missions.guidingQuestion: How did social categories relate to different everyday experiences?
missions.why: Social labels can affect opportunities, but people's dignity is equal. Named experiences prevent labels from replacing the people behind them.
missions.application: A source describes one woman's activity and social setting. What should we avoid?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Arts, Architecture, and Cultural Practices
missions.guidingQuestion: How do makers, use and adaptation help explain cultural works?
missions.why: Art and architecture involve people, purposes and choices. Studying those connections adds meaning beyond recognising a style.
missions.application: A cultural work combines features discussed in two source cards. What should we investigate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Continuity and Change in Filipino Society
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we explain continuity and change in a particular setting?
missions.why: The past does not change all at once for everyone. Comparing clear examples makes differences and continuing practices understandable.
missions.application: A community keeps a practice but changes the materials used. What does it illustrate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Communities Beyond Effective Spanish Control
missions.guidingQuestion: Why distinguish a colonial claim from effective control?
missions.why: A map label does not tell the whole story of authority. Local action and relationships help explain autonomy.
missions.application: A map marks an area as claimed while a source describes local decision-making. What should we investigate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Muslim Polities and Communities in Mindanao and Sulu
missions.guidingQuestion: How can leadership, trade and diplomacy help explain Muslim polities?
missions.why: Political communities have particular histories and relationships. A shared religion does not make every institution or experience identical.
missions.application: A record describes diplomacy by a named polity. Which explanation is careful?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Cordillera Communities and Indigenous Autonomy
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we investigate Cordillera autonomy without assuming isolation?
missions.why: Community actions and outside relationships both matter. Autonomy does not mean that people or their practices never changed.
missions.application: A source describes local decisions and outside exchange. What can coexist?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Diplomacy, Adaptation, Conflict, and Resistance
missions.guidingQuestion: How can negotiation, adaptation and conflict have different outcomes?
missions.why: Actions need to be understood in their circumstances. Naming a response is only the start of explaining it.
missions.application: Two sources describe negotiation and armed conflict. What should a comparison include?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Causes and Forms of Resistance
missions.guidingQuestion: How do we connect a grievance with a form of resistance?
missions.why: Understanding why people acted requires evidence about their concerns, actions and circumstances. One cause need not explain every case.
missions.application: A source links a particular demand with a protest. What is supported?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Early Regional Uprisings
missions.guidingQuestion: What makes a comparison between regional uprisings meaningful?
missions.why: Keeping events distinct helps us see both connections and differences in community action.
missions.application: Two uprising cards have different places and dates. What should a comparison do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Religious and Political Revolts
missions.guidingQuestion: How can religious and political concerns overlap in a movement?
missions.why: A movement can involve several concerns. Careful explanation avoids forcing complex actions into one simple label.
missions.application: A source describes concerns about both religious practice and authority. What should a report do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Leaders, Communities, and Regional Participation
missions.guidingQuestion: How do leaders, participants and affected residents differ?
missions.why: People contribute and experience events in different ways. Looking beyond a leader's name makes community history more meaningful.
missions.application: A source names a leader and some participants. What remains uncertain?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Outcomes and Historical Significance of Early Revolts
missions.guidingQuestion: How can an event matter even when its immediate aim was not achieved?
missions.why: Immediate outcomes and later remembrance answer different questions. Explaining both makes historical significance clearer.
missions.application: An uprising ended, but a later source remembers it. What should we distinguish?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Economic and Political Changes in the 18th Century
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we trace a change from a proposal to its effects?
missions.why: Historical change has stages. Dates and implementation evidence help us avoid treating a planned change as an instant result.
missions.application: A timeline lists a proposal, an order and later reports. What is a careful explanation?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Colonial Reforms and Their Effects
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we compare reform aims with experienced effects?
missions.why: A reform names a desired change. Examining effects helps us understand who benefited, who faced burdens and what remains unknown.
missions.application: A reform promises improvement, but two accounts report different experiences. What should we do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: International Events and the Spread of New Ideas
missions.guidingQuestion: How can political ideas travel without everyone responding in the same way?
missions.why: Access, reading and discussion matter to the spread of ideas. Circulation is not the same as universal agreement.
missions.application: A political text reaches some readers. What needs more evidence?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Local Grievances and Growing Political Awareness
missions.guidingQuestion: When does a local grievance support a wider political claim?
missions.why: A complaint and a broader shared aim are not identical. Connecting them requires evidence of what people said or did.
missions.application: A petition asks for a change in one locality. What can it establish?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Contributions and Lessons of Early Resistance
missions.guidingQuestion: How do we connect early resistance with later historical interpretations?
missions.why: Later people may draw lessons from earlier events. That does not mean everyone in the original event shared later aims.
missions.application: A later writer praises an early action. What should we keep separate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Participation of Different Regions and Communities
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we show regional participation without inventing universal participation?
missions.why: A wider history needs specific community evidence. Location, reported spread and participation are different claims.
missions.application: An account names activity in two places. What is supported?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Women and Indigenous Peoples in the Struggle
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we recognise women's and Indigenous people's contributions specifically?
missions.why: Recognising contributions means explaining actual actions, not assigning the same role to everyone with a shared identity.
missions.application: A source records a woman's public action. How should it be presented?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Unity, Division, and Collective Identity
missions.guidingQuestion: How can cooperation and disagreement both shape collective identity?
missions.why: Working together does not always mean complete agreement. Evidence about shared action and differences helps us understand belonging.
missions.application: A group cooperates on one request but disagrees on another issue. What follows?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Early Developments Toward Filipino National Consciousness
missions.guidingQuestion: How do particular sources help explain wider ideas of belonging?
missions.why: National consciousness developed through connected experiences and ideas. A careful account does not reduce it to one cause or universal agreement.
missions.application: Two dated sources express related public concerns. What should we explain?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Trade, Travel and the Sharing of Ideas
missions.guidingQuestion: How did connections create opportunities for sharing ideas, and who could access them?
missions.why: Travel and trade can enable contact, but costs and unequal access affect who participates. Ideas also depend on reading and discussion.
missions.application: A route becomes shorter, but travel still costs money. What is a careful conclusion?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Emerging Middle Class and Public Participation
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we explain a public contribution through someone's action?
missions.why: Education and resources can support public work. Explaining an actual action recognises initiative instead of assuming a social label explains everything.
missions.application: Women make an educational request and a later letter supports it. What should we distinguish?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Parish Reform and the Call for Fair Treatment
missions.guidingQuestion: Why did parish responsibilities and fair participation matter in reform efforts?
missions.why: Historical terms need their own context. Understanding roles helps explain the concern behind a reform request.
missions.application: A source uses secular clergy when discussing parish administration. What must we avoid?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Cavite and GOMBURZA: Events, Claims and Remembrance
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we distinguish events, accusations and later remembrance?
missions.why: A claim made by an authority is not automatically proof. Comparing accounts helps us examine injustice and historical interpretation carefully.
missions.application: An account accuses someone of involvement in an uprising. What else is needed?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Voices for Reform: La Solidaridad and La Liga Filipina
missions.guidingQuestion: How did publication and association express reform aims?
missions.why: Writing and organising are different forms of public participation. We can explain their goals without assuming every demand was achieved.
missions.application: A publication asks for representation. What does that establish?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Roles and Responsibilities in Early Filipino Communities
missions.guidingQuestion: How did roles and social positions affect people's responsibilities and choices?
missions.why: A community includes relationships and unequal opportunities as well as cooperation. Understanding roles must not mean ranking people's worth.
missions.application: A source describes one person's duties and restricted choices. What should a report explain?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Beliefs and Cultural Traditions
missions.guidingQuestion: How can traditions and sources help us understand beliefs respectfully?
missions.why: Beliefs, rituals and oral traditions can carry meaning. We can investigate sources without mocking beliefs or assuming every community practised alike.
missions.application: An account describes one community ritual. Which caption is careful?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Islam and Cultural Exchange
missions.guidingQuestion: How did travel, teaching and community relationships contribute to Islamic connections?
missions.why: Religious and cultural change involves people over time. A religion and a political institution should not be treated as the same thing.
missions.application: A timeline shows several contributions at different times. Which explanation fits?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Seafaring and the Balangay
missions.guidingQuestion: What can boat evidence tell us about skills and connections?
missions.why: Surviving boat parts help us investigate construction and travel. Recognising what they cannot show is part of understanding evidence.
missions.application: A recovered plank has a join but no passenger list. What can it help investigate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Trade Networks with Neighboring Asian Societies
missions.guidingQuestion: How can an object connect places without proving a direct journey?
missions.why: Goods may pass through several exchanges. Following evidence carefully helps us distinguish a network from an invented single voyage.
missions.application: A ceramic object was made in one region and later found elsewhere. What is supported?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Goods, Technologies, and Cultural Exchange
missions.guidingQuestion: What is the difference between exchanging a product and sharing a technique?
missions.why: An object and the knowledge used to make it are different. Communities can adapt ideas rather than simply copy everything.
missions.application: In a teaching case, a maker learns a technique but uses a local material. What happened?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Early Trading Centers and Maritime Communities
missions.guidingQuestion: What work and connections helped a maritime community function?
missions.why: A trading centre involves more than arriving boats. Supporting work and evidence from different places help us understand its wider connections.
missions.application: A port model shows arrivals, storage and local work. Which explanation uses the whole model?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Ancient Writing and Communication
missions.guidingQuestion: How do writing, language and translation give us different clues?
missions.why: A script is not the same as a language, and a translation involves interpretation. Comparing them helps us read historical claims carefully.
missions.application: A source card includes a written object, a transcription and a translation. Why label them separately?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Indigenous Arts, Crafts, and Technologies
missions.guidingQuestion: How do materials, purpose and skill shape a crafted object?
missions.why: Craft involves knowledge and choices. Studying its purpose helps us appreciate makers without treating cultural designs as free decoration to copy.
missions.application: A maker changes a material while keeping an object's purpose. What should we compare?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Regional Diversity and Cultural Traditions
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we compare traditions without stereotyping communities?
missions.why: Named examples help us appreciate diversity. A similarity does not erase differences, and one practice does not describe every person.
missions.application: Two source cards describe different cultural examples. What makes a fair comparison?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Contributions of Early Societies to Filipino Identity
missions.guidingQuestion: How can different heritage examples support a careful explanation of identity?
missions.why: Heritage includes diverse contributions. Connecting evidence helps us explain identity without pretending every community had one identical past.
missions.application: Your portfolio includes a boat detail and a writing source. What should your explanation do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: European Exploration and Its Motives
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we explain an expedition's motives without confusing them with its results?
missions.why: People may have several aims. Distinguishing aims from outcomes helps us examine decisions rather than assume plans always succeeded.
missions.application: An expedition record states a trading aim. What else is needed to describe its results?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Magellan's Expedition and Early Encounters
missions.guidingQuestion: How do different sources help us investigate an early encounter?
missions.why: An encounter involves more than one viewpoint. A source records what its author could observe or chose to report.
missions.application: Two accounts emphasise different parts of an encounter. What is a useful response?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Lapulapu and the Battle of Mactan
missions.guidingQuestion: What can evidence about Mactan help us explain about local action?
missions.why: People in the islands made decisions and acted in their own settings. Explaining their actions requires more than treating them as a background to an expedition.
missions.application: A source describes fighting at Mactan. Which claim needs separate evidence?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Expeditions After Magellan
missions.guidingQuestion: Why distinguish later expeditions rather than treat them as one event?
missions.why: Different expeditions had their own people, aims and outcomes. Keeping them separate helps us explain change over time.
missions.application: Two expedition cards have different dates and outcomes. What is the best summary?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Legazpi's Expedition
missions.guidingQuestion: How did an expedition relate to the establishment of colonial rule?
missions.why: Arrival, settlement and effective control are different developments. Distinguishing them makes historical change easier to explain.
missions.application: A timeline separates arrival from a later settlement. What should a report preserve?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Spanish Settlements in Cebu and Manila
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we compare the establishment of colonial settlements in different places?
missions.why: Settlements have particular settings and histories. Comparing them helps us avoid assuming every place changed in the same way.
missions.application: Two settlement cards describe Cebu and Manila. What makes the comparison careful?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Expansion of Colonial Control and Local Responses
missions.guidingQuestion: Why did colonial expansion meet different local responses?
missions.why: Communities responded through choices and circumstances. A map of claims does not by itself show what people experienced.
missions.application: A map marks a colonial claim, while a source describes local opposition. What should we distinguish?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Meaning, Motives, and Methods of Colonization
missions.guidingQuestion: What makes colonization different from a visit or exchange?
missions.why: Recognising imposed authority helps us examine power, methods and effects without confusing contact with control.
missions.application: A teaching case describes outside authorities imposing rules. Which idea does it illustrate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Governor-General and Central Government
missions.guidingQuestion: How did colonial offices relate to authority and actual decisions?
missions.why: An office title explains a role, not every action or outcome. Tracing decisions helps us understand institutions.
missions.application: An order was issued by an official. What needs separate evidence?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Local Government and Indigenous Leadership
missions.guidingQuestion: How did local leadership and colonial government interact?
missions.why: A local title or responsibility could connect different authorities. Particular evidence is needed to understand what changed for people.
missions.application: A local office has duties under colonial rules. What should we investigate?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Encomienda System and Tribute
missions.guidingQuestion: How can we distinguish an encomienda arrangement from owning land or people?
missions.why: Historical terms describe particular arrangements. Keeping authority, demands and obligations separate prevents misleading shortcuts.
missions.application: A source discusses tribute within an encomienda arrangement. What should a learner do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Reduccion and the Reorganization of Settlements
missions.guidingQuestion: How did reorganising settlements affect community life?
missions.why: Moving or concentrating settlements can affect access, work and relationships. A policy's aim does not describe every resident's experience.
missions.application: A settlement plan is compared with an account of daily life. Why use both?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Missionaries and the Spread of Christianity
missions.guidingQuestion: How did religious teaching spread, and how did communities respond?
missions.why: Religious change involves teaching, institutions and people's responses. Respect for beliefs goes together with careful use of historical sources.
missions.application: A source describes a mission and another describes a local response. What should we explain?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Patronato Real and Religious Authority
missions.guidingQuestion: How did royal and religious authority relate under the Patronato Real?
missions.why: Institutions can have connected roles without becoming identical. Following responsibilities helps us understand power.
missions.application: A diagram links royal and church responsibilities. Which explanation fits?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Changes in Beliefs, Practices, and Community Life
missions.guidingQuestion: How can a practice change while some meanings or activities continue?
missions.why: Continuity and change can happen together. Comparing particular examples is more useful than assuming complete replacement or no change.
missions.application: Two dated accounts describe a community practice. What should a comparison identify?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Indigenous Responses, Adaptation, and Resistance
missions.guidingQuestion: What different forms could community responses take?
missions.why: Adaptation, negotiation and resistance involve choices. Their meaning depends on the particular action and situation.
missions.application: A community negotiates over a demand. Which conclusion is careful?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Tribute and Colonial Taxation
missions.guidingQuestion: What is the difference between a tax demand, a payment and its burden?
missions.why: Records of demands and collections tell us different things. A household's experience needs evidence beyond the wording of a rule.
missions.application: A document lists tribute demanded but not payments collected. What can it establish?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Polo y Servicios and Bandala
missions.guidingQuestion: How do labour demands differ from demands for produce?
missions.why: Distinguishing kinds of demands helps us explain how policies affected work, supplies and households.
missions.application: One source asks for labour and another for products. What should a report do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Agriculture, Monopolies, and Economic Policies
missions.guidingQuestion: How can economic rules shape production and exchange?
missions.why: Policies can affect what people produce and how they exchange it. Stated purposes and experienced effects are different questions.
missions.application: A policy aims to change production. What is needed to explain its effects?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade
missions.guidingQuestion: What connected work and places made the galleon trade a network?
missions.why: A trading network includes routes, goods and labour, with different effects for different people. It is more than a line between ports.
missions.application: A route map and a work record describe the trade. Why compare them?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Effects of Colonial Economic Policies on Communities
missions.guidingQuestion: Why could one economic policy affect communities differently?
missions.why: Work, resources and local circumstances can change how a demand is experienced. A careful comparison keeps those differences visible.
missions.application: Two community accounts describe different effects of a policy. What should we do?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Life in the Barangay
missions.guidingQuestion: What makes people a community, beyond living near one another?
missions.why: Relationships, responsibilities and cooperation help us understand everyday life. Different communities could organise these in different ways.
missions.application: A fictional village scene shows shared work and different duties. Which claim fits?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Trade and Livelihood
missions.guidingQuestion: How do resources, skills and agreements make exchange useful?
missions.why: Food and useful objects come from work and resources. Exchange helps us explore how people with different products meet needs.
missions.application: One teaching community has fish and needs rice; another has rice and needs fish. What matters for exchange?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: The Philippines as an Archipelago: Location and Geography
missions.guidingQuestion: How can a map help explain connections between island communities?
missions.why: Geography helps us ask how people travelled and met their needs. A map gives clues, not a complete account of their lives.
missions.application: A map shows an inland river meeting the coast. Which explanation uses that clue?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Formation of the Philippine Islands: Scientific Explanations
missions.guidingQuestion: How do scientific models help explain changes to land?
missions.why: A process model helps us connect a change with a cause, while recognising that a classroom demonstration simplifies the real world.
missions.application: A model shows existing land uncovered as water level falls. What does that part show?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Archaeological Evidence of Early Human Presence
missions.guidingQuestion: What can a find and its recorded setting tell us about the past?
missions.why: History needs evidence. Recording a find and its setting helps people ask careful questions about earlier life.
missions.application: A tool has a photograph and a record of its site and layer. Why keep both?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.

missions.title: Early Population Movements and the Peopling of the Philippines
missions.guidingQuestion: Why compare different kinds of evidence about population movements?
missions.why: Language, objects and other evidence answer different questions. Comparing them helps us avoid treating one clue as a complete history of a people.
missions.application: Two communities have related language features. What is a careful next step?
missions.reviewStatus: Provisional author mapping, not DepEd approval or proof of learning.
